questions.question:
Consider the translation scheme shown below.

  • $S \rightarrow T\;R$
  • $R \rightarrow + T \{\text{print}(‘+’);\} R\mid \varepsilon$
  • $T  \rightarrow$ num $\{\text{print}$(num.val)$;\}$

Here num is a token that represents an integer and num.val represents the corresponding integer value. For an input string ‘$9 + 5 + 2$’, this translation scheme will print
questions.rawQuestionHtml:
Consider the translation scheme shown below.

  • $S \rightarrow T\;R$
  • $R \rightarrow + T \{\text{print}(‘+’);\} R\mid \varepsilon$

Here num is a token that represents an integer and num.val represents the corresponding integer value. For an input string ‘$9 + 5 + 2$’, this translation scheme will print

  2. $9 \ 5 + 2 +$

questions.subject: General Aptitude
questions.question:
Consider three IP networks $A, B$ and $C$. Host $H_A$ in network $A$ sends messages each containing $180$ bytes of application data to a host $H_C$ in network $C$. The $\text{TCP}$ layer prefixes $20$ byte header to the message.

This passes through an intermediate network $B$.The maximum packet size, including $20$ byte IP header, in each network is:

The network $A$ and $B$ are connected through a $1$ Mbps link, while $B$ and $C$
 are connected by a $512$ Kbps link (bps = bits per second).        

Assuming that the packets are correctly delivered, how many bytes, including headers, are delivered to the $IP$ layer at the destination for one application message, in the best case? Consider only data packets.

questions.subject: General Aptitude
questions.question:
Consider a three word machine instruction

$\text{ADD} A[R_0], @B$

The first operand (destination) $“A[R_0]”$ uses indexed addressing mode with $R_0$ as the index register. The second operand (source) $“@B”$ uses indirect addressing mode. $A$ and $B$ are memory addresses residing at the second and third words, respectively. The first word of the instruction specifies the opcode, the index register designation and the source and destination addressing modes. During execution of $\text{ADD}$ instruction, the two operands are added and stored in the destination (first operand).

The number of memory cycles needed during the execution cycle of the instruction is:

questions.title: GATE EC 2021 | EC Question: 1
questions.subject: Digital Circuits
questions.question: The minimum number of 2-to-1 multiplexers required to realize an arbitrary 4-to-1 multiplexer without any external logic gates is:
questions.explanation:
Step-by-Step Solution (Digital Circuits):

A 4-to-1 multiplexer has 2 select lines. Two 2-to-1 MUXes are used in the first stage driven by $S_0$, and one 2-to-1 MUX is used in the second stage driven by $S_1$. Total MUX count $= 2 + 1 = 3$.

questions.title: GATE EC 2021 | EC Question: 3
questions.subject: Control Systems
questions.question: The steady-state error $e_{ss}$ of a Type-1 unity feedback control system to a unit ramp input $r(t) = t \cdot u(t)$ is given by:
questions.explanation:
Step-by-Step Solution (Control Systems):

For a Type-1 system with unit ramp input: velocity error constant $K_v = \lim_{s \to 0} s G(s)$, and steady-state error $e_{ss} = \frac{1}{K_v}$.

questions.title: GATE EC 2021 | EC Question: 18
questions.subject: Electromagnetics & Antennas
questions.question: A lossless transmission line with characteristic impedance $Z_0 = 50\,\Omega$ is terminated in a load impedance $Z_L = 100\,\Omega$. The voltage reflection coefficient $\Gamma$ is:
questions.explanation:
Step-by-Step Solution (Electromagnetics & Antennas):

$\Gamma = \frac{Z_L - Z_0}{Z_L + Z_0} = \frac{100 - 50}{100 + 50} = \frac{50}{150} = +\frac{1}{3} = +0.333$.

questions.title: GATE EC 2021 | EC Question: 26
questions.subject: Communications & Information Theory
questions.question: According to Shannon's Channel Capacity theorem, the capacity $C$ of an additive white Gaussian noise (AWGN) channel with bandwidth $B$ and signal-to-noise ratio $\text{SNR} = S/N$ is:
questions.explanation:
Step-by-Step Solution (Communications & Information Theory):

Shannon-Hartley theorem states maximum error-free transmission capacity is $C = B \log_2 (1 + \text{SNR})$ bits/second.

questions.title: GATE EC 2021 | EC Question: 27
questions.subject: Communications & Information Theory
questions.question: An AM broadcast signal has a carrier power $P_c = 10\text{ kW}$ and modulation index $\mu = 0.8$. The total transmitted power $P_t = P_c \left(1 + \frac{\mu^2}{2}\right)$ (in $\text{kW}$) is ________.
questions.explanation:
Step-by-Step Solution (Communications & Information Theory):

$P_t = 10 \left(1 + \frac{0.8^2}{2}\right) = 10 \left(1 + \frac{0.64}{2}\right) = 10(1 + 0.32) = 13.2\text{ kW}$.

questions.title: GATE EC 2021 | EC Question: 35

questions.explanation:
Step-by-Step Solution (Electromagnetics & Antennas):

$\eta_0 = \sqrt{\frac{4\pi \times 10^{-7}}{8.854 \times 10^{-12}}} \approx 120\pi \approx 376.99 \approx 377\,\Omega$.

questions.title: GATE EC 2021 | EC Question: 42
questions.subject: Signals & Systems
questions.question: The continuous-time signal $x(t) = \cos(200\pi t) + \sin(600\pi t)$ is sampled. According to Nyquist criterion, the minimum sampling frequency $f_s$ (Nyquist rate, in Hz) required to avoid aliasing is ________.
questions.explanation:
Step-by-Step Solution (Signals & Systems):

The maximum angular frequency is $\omega_{\text{max}} = 600\pi\text{ rad/s} \implies f_{\text{max}} = \frac{600\pi}{2\pi} = 300\text{ Hz}$. The Nyquist rate is $f_s = 2 f_{\text{max}} = 2 \times 300 = 600\text{ Hz}$.
